The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# tailspin — A log file highlighter

tailspin highlights log files for easier reading. It can read from files or from stdin and supports printing
highlighted output to stdout or viewing interactively with a pager.

Usage examples:

- Read a file and view with the pager:
  tspin application.log

- Pipe into tspin and print to stdout:
  echo "hello" | tspin

- Follow a file (tail -f like behavior):
  tspin -f application.log

Installation:

- Homebrew: brew install tailspin
- Cargo: cargo install tailspin
- Package managers: check your platform's package repository

For more information, see the man page in the man/ directory (if present) and the example logs in example-logs/.

License:

This repository includes the project's license file (LICENCE or LICENSE) — see that file for license details.

\fI\\$2\fP <\\$1>\\$3
..

.  mso www.tmac

.    ad l
.  .
.  am MTO

.\}
.SH "NAME"
tspin \- A log file highlighter
.SH "SYNOPSIS"
.sp
\fBtspin\fP [\fIOPTION\fP]... [\fIFILE\fP]...
.SH "DESCRIPTION"
.sp
tailspin is a command line tool that highlights log files.
.SH "OPTIONS"
.sp
\fI\-f, \-\-follow\fP
.RS 4
Follow (tail) the contents of the file.
Always true when using the \fI\-\-follow\-command\fP flag.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-p, \-\-print\fP
.RS 4
Print the output to stdout instead of viewing the contents in the pager \fIless\fP.
Always true if using stdin.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-config\-path\fP \fBCONFIG_PATH\fP
.RS 4
Specify the path to a custom configuration file.
Defaults to \fBXDG_CONFIG_HOME/tailspin/theme.toml\fP or \fB~/.config/tailspin/theme.toml\fP if not set.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-e, \-\-exec\fP \fBCOMMAND\fP
.RS 4
Run command and view the output in a pager.
The command traps the interrupt signal to allow for cancelling and resuming follow mode while inside \fIless\fP.
.sp
.B Example:
.br
.sp
.if n .RS 4
.nf
.fam C
tspin \-\-listen\-command \*(Aqkubectl logs \-f pod_name\*(Aq
.fam
.fi

.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-highlight\fP \fBCOLOR1\fP:\fIword1,word2,...\fP \fBCOLOR2\fP:\fIword3,word4,...\fP
.RS 4
Highlight the provided comma\-separated words in the specified color.
Possible colors are red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, and cyan.
.sp
.B Example:
.br
.sp
.if n .RS 4
.nf
.fam C
tspin logfile.txt \-\-highlight red:error,fail \-\-highlight green:success,ok
.fam
.fi
.if n .RE
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-enable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP
.RS 4
Disable all highlighting groups except the ones specified.
Comma separated list of groups.
Cannot be used with \fB\-\-disable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-disable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP
.RS 4
Disable the specified highlighting groups.
Comma separated list of groups.
Cannot be used with \fB\-\-enable=[HIGHLIGHT_GROUP]\fP.
.RE
.sp
\fI\-\-disable\-builtin\-keywords\fP
.RS 4
Disables the highlighting of all builtin keyword groups (booleans, severity and REST).
.RE

\fBTAILSPIN_PAGER\fP

.RE

\fBless\fP(1), \fBtail\fP(1)

"""Rendering and recognition of common fragments in diagnostic output.

Each recognizer owns the pieces that it finds. Later recognizers work only on
unclaimed pieces, so lower-level tokens never repaint a larger structure.
"""
import re
import json
import math
import ipaddress
from dataclasses import dataclass

COLORS = {'default':39,'black':30,'red':31,'green':32,'yellow':33,
          'blue':34,'magenta':35,'cyan':36,'white':37,
          'bright_black':90,'bright_red':91,'bright_green':92,
          'bright_yellow':93,'bright_blue':94,'bright_magenta':95,
          'bright_cyan':96,'bright_white':97}

@dataclass
class Style:
    fg: str = None
    bg: str = None
    bold: bool = False
    faint: bool = False
    italic: bool = False
    underline: bool = False

    def paint(self, text, pad=False):
        codes = []
        for name, code in [('bold',1),('faint',2),('italic',3),('underline',4)]:
            if getattr(self,name):
                codes.append(str(code))
        if self.bg is not None:
            codes.append(str(COLORS[self.bg]+10))
        if self.fg is not None:
            codes.append(str(COLORS[self.fg]))
        if not codes:
            return text
        if pad and self.bg is not None:
            text = ' '+text+' '
        return '\x1b['+';'.join(codes)+'m'+text+'\x1b[0m'


def default_styles():
    return {
        'numbers': {'number':Style(fg='cyan')},
        'dates': {'date':Style(fg='magenta'),'time':Style(fg='blue'),
                  'separator':Style(faint=True),'zone':Style(fg='red')},
        'ip_addresses':{'number':Style(fg='blue',italic=True),
                        'letter':Style(fg='magenta',italic=True),'separator':Style(fg='red')},
        'urls': {'http':Style(fg='red',faint=True),'https':Style(fg='green',faint=True),
                 'host':Style(fg='blue',faint=True),'path':Style(fg='blue'),
                 'symbols':Style(fg='red'),'query_params_key':Style(fg='magenta'),'query_params_value':Style(fg='cyan')},
        'key_value_pairs':{'key':Style(faint=True),'separator':Style(fg='white')},
        'paths':{'segment':Style(fg='green'),'separator':Style(fg='yellow')},
        'pointers':{'number':Style(fg='blue',italic=True),'letter':Style(fg='magenta',italic=True),
                    'x':Style(fg='red'),'separator':Style(faint=True),'separator_token':'•'},
        'uuids':{'number':Style(fg='blue',italic=True),'letter':Style(fg='magenta',italic=True),
                 'dash':Style(fg='red')},
        'processes':{'name':Style(fg='yellow'),'id':Style(fg='cyan'),'bracket':Style(fg='red')},
        'quotes':{'quotes_token':'"','style':Style(fg='yellow')},
        'json':{'key':Style(faint=True),'colon':Style(faint=True),'comma':Style(faint=True),
                'square_bracket':Style(faint=True),'curly_bracket':Style(faint=True),

# Deliberately ASCII: in log records the punctuation surrounding an identifier

ASCII = re.ASCII
DAY = r'(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])'

        config='[[keywords]]\nwords=["hello"]\nstyle={fg="black",bg="green"}'

class ConfigTests(unittest.TestCase):

        config='[[keywords]]\nwords=["hello"]\nstyle={fg="black",bg="green"}'
        self.assertEqual(self.render(config,'hello'),'\x1b[42;30m hello \x1b[0m')

import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


class CLITests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.env=dict(os.environ,XDG_CONFIG_HOME=self.temp.name,NO_COLOR='1')

    def run_program(self,args=(),data=b''):
        return subprocess.run([str(ROOT/'executable')]+list(args),input=data,
                              capture_output=True,env=self.env,timeout=5)

    def test_version(self):
        p=self.run_program(['--version'])
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,b'tspin 5.6.0\n',b''))

    def test_stdin_final_line(self):
        p=self.run_program(data=b'hello')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,b'hello\n')

    def test_stdin_crlf(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_program(data=b'hello\r\n').stdout,b'hello\r\n')

    def test_empty_stdin(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_program().stdout,b'')

    def test_invalid_utf8(self):
        p=self.run_program(data=b'\xff\n')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,'Error:   × stream did not contain valid UTF-8\n\n'.encode())

    def test_filters(self):
        p=self.run_program(['--enable','numbers','--disable-builtin-keywords'],b'INFO 42\n')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,b'INFO \x1b[36m42\x1b[0m\n')

    def test_conflicting_filters(self):
        p=self.run_program(['--enable','numbers','--disable','dates'])
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,'Error:   × cannot both enable and disable highlighters\n\n'.encode())

    def test_argument_error(self):
        p=self.run_program(['--bad'])
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,("error: unexpected argument '--bad' found\n\n"
                         "  tip: to pass '--bad' as a value, use '-- --bad'\n\n"
                         "Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [FILE]\n\n"
                         "For more information, try '--help'.\n").encode())

    def test_print_file_partial_tail(self):
        pth=Path(self.temp.name)/'log'
        pth.write_bytes(b'hello\r\nunfinished')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_program(['-p',str(pth)]).stdout,b'hello\n')

    def test_empty_file(self):
        pth=Path(self.temp.name)/'log';pth.write_bytes(b'')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_program(['-p',str(pth)]).stdout,b'\n')

    def test_pager_file_partial_tail(self):
        pth=Path(self.temp.name)/'log';pth.write_bytes(b'hello\nunfinished')
        p=self.run_program([str(pth),'--pager','cat [FILE]'])
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,b'hello\nunfinished\n',b''))

    def test_stdin_takes_precedence_over_command(self):
        p=self.run_program(['--exec','printf ignored'],b'hello\n')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,b'hello\n')

    def test_explicit_theme(self):
        pth=Path(self.temp.name)/'theme.toml';pth.write_text('[numbers]\nnumber={fg="red"}')
        p=self.run_program(['--config-path',str(pth)],b'42\n')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,b'\x1b[31m42\x1b[0m\n')

    def test_xdg_theme(self):
        parent=Path(self.temp.name)/'tailspin';parent.mkdir()
        (parent/'theme.toml').write_text('[numbers]\nnumber={fg="blue"}')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_program(data=b'42\n').stdout,b'\x1b[34m42\x1b[0m\n')


if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()
